evidence.docstring:
Each file is flattened into a stream of AST tokens: the node type, plus
attribute names (``.infer``) and constant *types*.

extractor: new: the token kinds pyeye.duplication.tokenize keeps (node type, Attribute.attr, Constant value type) and drops (Name ids, def/arg names, docstrings, imports)
problem: Says 'Local names, literal values, docstrings, comments and imports are ignored', implying other names are kept. The tokenizer keeps only node types, attribute names and constant types: every bare Name is erased, so two functions that call entirely different globals or builtins (validate/scale/... vs sorted/len/...) match as one clone (verified with a two-file run: 46-token family). That under-warns Claude about false positives, the very thing the next bullet asks it to judge.
replacement: Bind the normalisation rule as a fact (what is kept: node types, attribute names, constant types). Keep only the consequence in prose: 'so a copy with renamed variables still matches, and so can code that calls different functions with the same shape; read both regions.'

problem: The review flag table's Flag column, the dismiss synopsis and the dismiss bullet list hand-write every flag name (`--root`, `--min-tokens`, `--max-occurrences`, `--state`, `--today`, `--json`, `--family`, `--reason`, `--date`, `--review-after`) although each is a duplication.flag.* fact; the Default column next to it already binds its values. A renamed flag would leave the table stale with check still green.
replacement: Bind each Flag-column cell and each flag in the dismiss synopsis and bullets to its duplication.flag.* fact (as the Default column binds duplication.default.*), and the command names `review`/`dismiss` to duplication.command.*.

evidence.docstring:
A site inside
one class keeps its method endpoints, unless one of them is also in a
cross-class site: then it joins that class's family too.

problem: Says 'a copy inside one class stays with its methods, and a copy between a function and a class method is not folded into the class'. Both have an exception the code implements: when the method also takes part in a cross-class pair, that end becomes its class node, so the intra-class copy and the function-to-method copy join the class's family. Verified: f() copied into A.m and B.m gives ONE family of 3 sites, not a separate f<->A.m family.
replacement: A family groups copies that connect: all the copies between two classes are one family, and any other copy of a method that is in such a pair (from a function, or within its class) joins that family too. Otherwise a copy inside one class stays with its methods, and a function-to-method copy is not folded into the class.
route_reason: Grouping is an algorithm over a run's sites, not a static value an extractor can read, and executed examples run MCP tools, not this CLI.

evidence.docstring:
``new_sites`` are the uncovered sites (only they
  are shown) and ``new_locations`` the locations no dismissal names, which
  is empty for a new copy bridging two dismissed families.

problem: Says a re-surfaced family shows 'Only the new or changed members'. The code shows only the uncovered sites (pairs), and for a new copy bridging two dismissed families there is no new member at all (new_locations is empty) yet the bridging site is shown. It also disagrees with the same page's 'Only the new sites are shown' under What a Result Means.
replacement: Only the new sites are shown (a bridging copy can add a site with no new member).
route_reason: Which sites a re-surfaced family shows depends on a run's dismissal state, not a static value an extractor can read; executed examples run MCP tools, not this CLI.
